entities.summary: Carneades (b. 212 BCE, Cyrene) was a prominent Stoic philosopher and thinker of the Classical era, active in Cyrene, who significantly contributed to the development of Stoicism and its influence on Western philosophy. A student of the famous Stoic philosopher Polemon of Attica, Carneades was one of the most influential Stoic philosophers of his time, known for his rigorous intellectual pursuits and his role in shaping the Stoic school of thought. His work had a lasting impact on Western philosophy, influencing prominent thinkers such as Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius, and continuing to shape philosophical debates to this day.
